verdict.rationale: Community reports describe a first-party 'Portable Computer' offering that runs Perplexity's Computer harness locally on user-supplied NVIDIA DGX Spark hardware. That is a product-provided form of self-hosting, but a limited one: the same reports say it is closed source, requires a Pro or Max subscription, depends on Perplexity's orchestrator escalating work to the cloud, and is tied to one expensive hardware platform. The first-party docs cover only the cloud-hosted Computer and its hosted MCP endpoint. Missing for 10: first-party documentation of the self-hosted/local deployment, fully self-contained operation without cloud or subscription dependency, support for general hardware, and hands-on corroboration of a working local install.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: "Portable Computer" lets you run that harness locally, but you must bring your own NVIDIA DGX Spark.
